elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates against all required categories of third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause requires SFJ to “indemnify and hold” the PB Indemnified Parties harmless, but contains no express duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor’s services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph indemnifies the PB Indemnified Parties, which include PB and its Affiliates, against third-party claims alleging that SFJ-provided “services, materials or deliverables” infringe or misappropriate third-party IP.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: No SFJ indemnity trigger expressly covers SFJ’s breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no indemnity trigger for a data breach or security incident caused by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.1(a) covers third-party claims arising from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of SFJ, its Affiliates, or their Permitted Third Parties in performing SFJ’s obligations.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires the indemnified party to give notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No claims-notice procedure appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure gives the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No defense or settlement-control provision appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation by the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.2 does not identify Customer-provided content as an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12.1.2 does not expressly provide an indemnity for PB’s breach of law.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity is limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: PB’s indemnity remains materially broader, including claims involving a Product supplied by PB, PB’s material contractual or Protocol breach, Product infringement, subject injuries, and commercialization.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-provided services, materials, or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly provides this indemnity to the PB Indemnified Parties for claims involving SFJ-provided services, materials, or deliverables.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer’s modifications.
elements.evidence: The indemnity excludes claims to the extent arising from “PB’s modification of such items.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer’s combination of the covered items with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnity excludes claims arising from “PB’s combination of such items with items not supplied by SFJ.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Vendor’s compliance with Customer’s specifications.
elements.evidence: The indemnity excludes claims arising from “SFJ’s compliance with PB’s specifications.”

elements.element: For an infringing item, Vendor must procure Customer’s right to continue using it.
elements.evidence: SFJ must “procure for PB the right to continue using the infringing item.”

elements.element: For an infringing item, Vendor may modify it so that it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The remedies expressly permit SFJ to “modify” the item so that it is non-infringing.

elements.element: For an infringing item, Vendor may replace it with a non-infringing item.
elements.evidence: The remedies expressly permit SFJ to “replace it so that it is non-infringing.”

elements.element: If procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable on commercially reasonable terms, Vendor must refund the applicable amounts paid by Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause requires a refund of amounts paid for the item if none of the preceding remedies is available on commercially reasonable terms.

elements.element: Vendor’s liability under the IP indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Liability under the added IP-indemnity paragraph is capped at three times the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ during the twelve months preceding the claim, implementing a 3× annualized-fees cap.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback by adding a third-party Vendor IP indemnity, all three customary exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and a 3× twelve-month payment cap. Narrowing PB’s infringement indemnity avoids making PB indemnify SFJ for SFJ’s own performance-related infringement and is reasonably related to the fallback. The preferred position is not reached because there is no defense duty, breach-of-law or data-breach indemnity, claims procedure, or appropriately limited Customer indemnity. Drafting quality is reduced by the rendered clause’s incomplete ending, skipped subparagraphs, and pre-existing grammatical defects.
